<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Influence-Preserving Low-Rank Approximation for Influence Functions</h3>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We now extend the analysis from the simplified TracIn score to Influence Functions (IF). IFs refine the influence measure by incorporating the inverse Hessian of the loss, which accounts for the local curvature of the optimization landscape.
The influence of a training sample <math id="A5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> on a validation smaple <math id="A5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> is defined as:</p>
<table id="A5.Ex22" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.Ex22.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{\text{IF}}(z,z^{\prime})\triangleq-\nabla_{\theta}L(z^{\prime};\theta)^{\top}\mathcal{H}(\theta)^{-1}\nabla_{\theta}L(z;\theta)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><mtext>IF</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">−</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><mi>L</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><mi>L</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{\text{IF}}(z,z^{\prime})\triangleq-\nabla_{\theta}L(z^{\prime};\theta)^{\top}\mathcal{H}(\theta)^{-1}\nabla_{\theta}L(z;\theta).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.p1.2" class="ltx_p">To analyze the contribution of a single weight matrix <math id="A5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> at layer <math id="A5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>, we consider its vectorized form <math id="A5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{\ell}\triangleq\text{vec}(W_{\ell})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mtext>vec</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\ell}\triangleq\text{vec}(W_{\ell})</annotation></semantics></math>. The gradient of the loss with respect to these vectorized parameters is the outer product of the upstream gradients <math id="A5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{\ell}(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{\ell}(z)</annotation></semantics></math> and the inputs <math id="A5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{\ell}(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{\ell}(z)</annotation></semantics></math>. Using the identity <math id="A5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{vec}(ab^{\top})=b\otimes a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext>vec</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{vec}(ab^{\top})=b\otimes a</annotation></semantics></math>, this gradient is:</p>
<table id="A5.Ex23" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.Ex23.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{w_{\ell}}L(z;\theta)=\text{vec}\big(\delta_{\ell}(z)h_{\ell}(z)^{\top}\big)=h_{\ell}(z)\otimes\delta_{\ell}(z)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></msub><mi>L</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>vec</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{w_{\ell}}L(z;\theta)=\text{vec}\big(\delta_{\ell}(z)h_{\ell}(z)^{\top}\big)=h_{\ell}(z)\otimes\delta_{\ell}(z).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Following previous works <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Martens and Grosse, 2015</a>; <a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Grosse et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, we make key simplifying assumptions about the Hessian’s structure. We assume the full Hessian matrix is block-diagonal, with each block corresponding to the parameters of a single layer, and that within each layer <math id="A5.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>, the inputs <math id="A5.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{\ell}(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{\ell}(z)</annotation></semantics></math> are independent of the upstream gradients <math id="A5.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{\ell}(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{\ell}(z)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">These assumptions allow us to define a tractable surrogate Hessian <math id="A5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathcal{H}}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathcal{H}}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> for layer <math id="A5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> as the expected outer product of its vectorized gradients:</p>

<p id="A5.p2.2" class="ltx_p">Here, <math id="A5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{h,\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{h,\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\delta,\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\delta,\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> are the second moment matrices of the activations and upstream gradients for layer <math id="A5.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively. Leveraging the property that <math id="A5.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(A\otimes B)^{-1}=A^{-1}\otimes B^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(A\otimes B)^{-1}=A^{-1}\otimes B^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, the inverse is given by <math id="A5.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathcal{H}}_{\ell}^{-1}=C_{h,\ell}^{-1}\otimes C_{\delta,\ell}^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathcal{H}}_{\ell}^{-1}=C_{h,\ell}^{-1}\otimes C_{\delta,\ell}^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The contribution of layer <math id="A5.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> to the influence is then defined as:</p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.Ex31.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=-\langle\tilde{h}_{\ell}(z^{\prime}),\tilde{h}_{\ell}(z)\rangle_{F}\,\langle\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z^{\prime}),\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z)\rangle_{F}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>δ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>δ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=-\langle\tilde{h}_{\ell}(z^{\prime}),\tilde{h}_{\ell}(z)\rangle_{F}\,\langle\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z^{\prime}),\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z)\rangle_{F},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.p2.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A5.p2.m9" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\tilde{h}_{\ell}=C_{h,\ell}^{-1/2}h_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><msub><mrow></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>h</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{h}_{\ell}=C_{h,\ell}^{-1/2}h_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.p2.m10" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}=C_{\delta,\ell}^{-1/2}\delta_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>δ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><msub><mrow></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>δ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}=C_{\delta,\ell}^{-1/2}\delta_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> are reweighting matrices.</p>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">An Objective for Preserving Influence Functions</h5>

<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To preserve the influences under low-rank approximation, we penalize the compression error using a norm aligned with the reweighting induced by <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{h,\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{h,\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\delta,\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\delta,\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>. We assume that <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{h,\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{h,\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\delta,\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\delta,\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> are symmetric positive definite. The objective is to find an error matrix <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{\ell}=W_{\ell}-\widehat{W}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>W</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{\ell}=W_{\ell}-\widehat{W}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> that minimizes the following term:</p>
<table id="A5.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.E11.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\min_{\widehat{W_{\ell}}\;\text{s.t.}\;\operatorname{rank}(\widehat{W_{\ell}})\leq r}\;\big\|\,C_{\delta,\ell}^{-1/2}\,(W_{\ell}-\widehat{W_{\ell}})\,C_{h,\ell}^{-1/2}\,\big\|_{F}^{2}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><munder><mi>min</mi><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><msub><mi>W</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0.280em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>s.t.</mtext><mo lspace="0.447em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>rank</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><msub><mi>W</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></munder><mo mathsize="1.200em" rspace="0.337em">∥</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><msub><mi>W</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>^</mo></mover><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><msubsup><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="1.200em" rspace="0.0835em">∥</mo><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0.0835em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\min_{\widehat{W_{\ell}}\;\text{s.t.}\;\operatorname{rank}(\widehat{W_{\ell}})\leq r}\;\big\|\,C_{\delta,\ell}^{-1/2}\,(W_{\ell}-\widehat{W_{\ell}})\,C_{h,\ell}^{-1/2}\,\big\|_{F}^{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">We now demonstrate that minimizing this objective effectively controls the expected change in the influence score. Our theoretical guarantees rely on the following assumptions.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<ul id="A5.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A5.I1.ix1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><span id="A5.I1.ix1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(B1)</span></span> 
<div id="A5.I1.ix1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.I1.ix1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">(Finite moments). <math id="A5.I1.ix1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}_{z}[\|\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z)\|\,\|\tilde{h}_{\ell}(z)\|]" display="inline" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mover stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}_{z}[\|\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z)\|\,\|\tilde{h}_{\ell}(z)\|]</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.I1.ix1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}_{z^{\prime}}[\|\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z^{\prime})\|\,\|\tilde{h}_{\ell}(z^{\prime})\|]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>δ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}_{z^{\prime}}[\|\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z^{\prime})\|\,\|\tilde{h}_{\ell}(z^{\prime})\|]</annotation></semantics></math> are finite.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A5.I1.ix2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><span id="A5.I1.ix2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(B2)</span></span> 
<div id="A5.I1.ix2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.I1.ix2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">(Backward smoothness). Let <math id="A5.I1.ix2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{\delta}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>δ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{\delta}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the upstream gradient under <math id="A5.I1.ix2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{W}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>W</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{W}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>. There exists a measurable function <math id="A5.I1.ix2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K(\cdot)\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K(\cdot)\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math> such that
<math id="A5.I1.ix2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\Delta\delta_{\ell}(z)\|\leq K(z)\,\|E_{\ell}\|_{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\Delta\delta_{\ell}(z)\|\leq K(z)\,\|E_{\ell}\|_{F}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A5.I1.ix2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\delta_{\ell}(z)\triangleq\widehat{\delta}_{\ell}(z)-\delta_{\ell}(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>δ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\delta_{\ell}(z)\triangleq\widehat{\delta}_{\ell}(z)-\delta_{\ell}(z)</annotation></semantics></math>, and
<math id="A5.I1.ix2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}_{z}[K(z)\|\tilde{h}_{\ell}(z)\|],\;\mathbb{E}_{z^{\prime}}[K(z^{\prime})\|\tilde{h}_{\ell}(z^{\prime})\|]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.447em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}_{z}[K(z)\|\tilde{h}_{\ell}(z)\|],\;\mathbb{E}_{z^{\prime}}[K(z^{\prime})\|\tilde{h}_{\ell}(z^{\prime})\|]</annotation></semantics></math> are finite.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A5.I1.ix3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><span id="A5.I1.ix3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(B3)</span></span> 
<div id="A5.I1.ix3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.I1.ix3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">(Quadratic remainder). There exists <math id="A5.I1.ix3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> such that for all <math id="A5.I1.ix3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{W}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>W</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{W}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> with</p>
<table id="A5.Ex32" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.Ex32.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\big\|C_{\delta,\ell}^{-1/2}\,(W_{\ell}-\widehat{W}_{\ell})\,C_{h,\ell}^{-1/2}\big\|_{F}\;\leq\;\rho," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo mathsize="1.200em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>W</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><msub><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="1.200em" rspace="0.0835em">∥</mo><mi>F</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.0835em" rspace="0.558em">≤</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\big\|C_{\delta,\ell}^{-1/2}\,(W_{\ell}-\widehat{W}_{\ell})\,C_{h,\ell}^{-1/2}\big\|_{F}\;\leq\;\rho,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.I1.ix3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">the Taylor remainder <math id="A5.I1.ix3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R(z,z^{\prime})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R(z,z^{\prime})</annotation></semantics></math> in the perturbation of <math id="A5.I1.ix3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{\text{IF},W_{\ell}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>I</mi><mrow><mtext>IF</mtext><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{\text{IF},W_{\ell}}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfies</p>
<table id="A5.Ex33" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<div id="A5.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A5.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition E.1</span></span><span id="A5.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A5.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="A5.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> be perturbed to <math id="A5.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{W}_{\ell}=W_{\ell}-E_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>W</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{W}_{\ell}=W_{\ell}-E_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>. Under </span>(B1)<span id="A5.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">–</span>(B3)<span id="A5.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, there exists a finite, data-dependent constant <math id="A5.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\kappa}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>κ</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\kappa}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> such that</span></p>

<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.1" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">Recall that the layer-<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> influence is given by</span></p>
<table id="A5.Ex34" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.Ex34.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{\text{IF},W_{\ell}}(z,z^{\prime})=-\langle\tilde{h}_{\ell}(z^{\prime}),\tilde{h}_{\ell}(z)\rangle_{F}\,\langle\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z^{\prime}),\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z)\rangle_{F}." <p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\Delta\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z)\triangleq C_{\delta,\ell}^{-1/2}\big(\widehat{\delta}_{\ell}(z)-\delta_{\ell}(z)\big)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>δ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≜</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>δ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z)\triangleq C_{\delta,\ell}^{-1/2}\big(\widehat{\delta}_{\ell}(z)-\delta_{\ell}(z)\big)</annotation></semantics></math> denote the change in the reweighted upstream gradient. The total change in influence consists of a first-order Taylor expansion term, <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta I_{\text{IF}}^{(1)}(z,z^{\prime})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>I</mi><mtext>IF</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta I_{\text{IF}}^{(1)}(z,z^{\prime})</annotation></semantics></math>, and a remainder term <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R(z,z^{\prime})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R(z,z^{\prime})</annotation></semantics></math>. The first-order term is:</span></p>

<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.3.1" class="ltx_text">By taking the expectation over <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z,z^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z,z^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>, applying the triangle and Cauchy–Schwarz inequalities, and using the independence of <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>, we can bound the expected first-order change:</span></p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" accent="true"><mi>δ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}_{z,z^{\prime}}\!\big[|\Delta I_{\text{IF}}^{(1)}|\big]\leq M_{\mathrm{tr}}\,\mathbb{E}_{z^{\prime}}\!\big[\|\Delta\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z^{\prime})\|\,\|\tilde{h}_{\ell}(z^{\prime})\|\big]+M_{\mathrm{val}}\,\mathbb{E}_{z}\!\big[\|\Delta\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z)\|\,\|\tilde{h}_{\ell}(z)\|\big],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.4.1" class="ltx_text">where <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{\mathrm{tr}}=\mathbb{E}_{z}[\|\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z)\|\,\|\tilde{h}_{\ell}(z)\|]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>tr</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>δ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{\mathrm{tr}}=\mathbb{E}_{z}[\|\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z)\|\,\|\tilde{h}_{\ell}(z)\|]</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{\mathrm{val}}=\mathbb{E}_{z^{\prime}}[\|\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z^{\prime})\|\,\|\tilde{h}_{\ell}(z^{\prime})\|]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>δ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{\mathrm{val}}=\mathbb{E}_{z^{\prime}}[\|\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z^{\prime})\|\,\|\tilde{h}_{\ell}(z^{\prime})\|]</annotation></semantics></math> are finite by Assumption (B1).
Our main task is to bound the expectation <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}_{z}\!\big[\|\Delta\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z)\|\,\|\tilde{h}_{\ell}(z)\|\big]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>δ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}_{z}\!\big[\|\Delta\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z)\|\,\|\tilde{h}_{\ell}(z)\|\big]</annotation></semantics></math> in terms of the objective function. Let <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m11" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\widetilde{E}_{\ell}\triangleq C_{\delta,\ell}^{-1/2}E_{\ell}C_{h,\ell}^{-1/2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>E</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><msub><mrow></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>≜</mo><mi>C</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>E</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mi>C</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{E}_{\ell}\triangleq C_{\delta,\ell}^{-1/2}E_{\ell}C_{h,\ell}^{-1/2}</annotation></semantics></math>. We first establish a pointwise bound on <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\Delta\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z)\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>δ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\Delta\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z)\|</annotation></semantics></math> using Assumption (B2).</span></p>

<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.5.1" class="ltx_text">Next, we relate <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|E_{\ell}\|_{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|E_{\ell}\|_{F}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\widetilde{E}_{\ell}\|_{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>E</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\widetilde{E}_{\ell}\|_{F}</annotation></semantics></math>. From the definition of <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{E}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>E</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{E}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{\ell}=C_{\delta,\ell}^{1/2}\widetilde{E}_{\ell}C_{h,\ell}^{1/2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>E</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{\ell}=C_{\delta,\ell}^{1/2}\widetilde{E}_{\ell}C_{h,\ell}^{1/2}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>

<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.6.1" class="ltx_text">Recall that <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{h,\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{h,\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\delta,\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\delta,\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> are all symmetric and positive definite, combining these inequalities yields a pointwise bound on <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\Delta\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z)\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>δ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\Delta\tilde{\delta}_{\ell}(z)\|</annotation></semantics></math> in terms of <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\widetilde{E}_{\ell}\|_{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>E</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\widetilde{E}_{\ell}\|_{F}</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></p>

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.Ex39.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle\leq K(z)\|C_{\delta,\ell}^{-1/2}\|_{2}\left(\|C_{\delta,\ell}^{1/2}\|_{2}\|\widetilde{E}_{\ell}\|_{F}\|C_{h,\ell}^{1/2}\|_{2}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>K</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.0835em">∥</mo><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.0835em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>E</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.0835em">∥</mo><mi>F</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.0835em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\leq K(z)\|C_{\delta,\ell}^{-1/2}\|_{2}\left(\|C_{\delta,\ell}^{1/2}\|_{2}\|\widetilde{E}_{\ell}\|_{F}\|C_{h,\ell}^{1/2}\|_{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<tbody id="A5.Ex40"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.7" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.7.1" class="ltx_text">where <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{cond}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>cond</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{cond}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\max}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\max}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> denote the condition number and maximum eigenvalue, respectively. Let us define the data-dependent scaling constant <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S\triangleq\sqrt{\text{cond}(C_{\delta,\ell})\lambda_{\max}(C_{h,\ell})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>≜</mo><msqrt><mrow><mtext>cond</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S\triangleq\sqrt{\text{cond}(C_{\delta,\ell})\lambda_{\max}(C_{h,\ell})}</annotation></semantics></math>.
We now use this result to bound the expectation term:</span></p>

<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.8" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.8.1" class="ltx_text">By Assumption (B2), the expectations <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m24" class="ltx_Math" <p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.10" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.10.1" class="ltx_text">Using Assumption (B3), for perturbations satisfying <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\widetilde{E}_{\ell}\|_{F}\leq\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>E</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mi>ρ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\widetilde{E}_{\ell}\|_{F}\leq\rho</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}_{z,z^{\prime}}[|R|]\leq c_{\mathrm{rem}}\|\widetilde{E}_{\ell}\|_{F}^{2}\leq c_{\mathrm{rem}}\rho\|\widetilde{E}_{\ell}\|_{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>rem</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>E</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>rem</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>E</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}_{z,z^{\prime}}[|R|]\leq c_{\mathrm{rem}}\|\widetilde{E}_{\ell}\|_{F}^{2}\leq c_{\mathrm{rem}}\rho\|\widetilde{E}_{\ell}\|_{F}</annotation></semantics></math>. Combining the terms gives the final result:</span></p>
<table id="A5.Ex46" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.Ex46.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}_{z,z^{\prime}}\!\big|\Delta I_{\text{IF},W_{\ell}}\big|\leq\left(S(M_{\mathrm{tr}}\kappa_{\mathrm{val}}+M_{\mathrm{val}}\kappa_{\mathrm{tr}})+c_{\mathrm{rem}}\rho\right)\|\widetilde{E}_{\ell}\|_{F}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mrow><mtext>IF</mtext><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>tr</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>κ</mi><mi>val</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>κ</mi><mi>tr</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>rem</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ρ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>E</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}_{z,z^{\prime}}\!\big|\Delta I_{\text{IF},W_{\ell}}\big|\leq\left(S(M_{\mathrm{tr}}\kappa_{\mathrm{val}}+M_{\mathrm{val}}\kappa_{\mathrm{tr}})+c_{\mathrm{rem}}\rho\right)\|\widetilde{E}_{\ell}\|_{F}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.11" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.11.1" class="ltx_text">This proves the proposition with the constant <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\kappa}\triangleq S(M_{\mathrm{tr}}\kappa_{\mathrm{val}}+M_{\mathrm{val}}\kappa_{\mathrm{tr}})+c_{\mathrm{rem}}\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>κ</mi></msub><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>tr</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>κ</mi><mi>val</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>κ</mi><mi>tr</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>rem</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ρ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\kappa}\triangleq S(M_{\mathrm{tr}}\kappa_{\mathrm{val}}+M_{\mathrm{val}}\kappa_{\mathrm{tr}})+c_{\mathrm{rem}}\rho</annotation></semantics></math>, which is finite and depends on data properties but not on the specific perturbation <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>E</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Efficient Implementation via Probe-Based Approximation and Core SVD</h3>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The theoretical solution presented in the main text requires computing, inverting, and taking the square root of the second moment matrices <math id="A6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{h,\ell}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{\ell}\times n_{\ell}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{h,\ell}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{\ell}\times n_{\ell}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\delta,\ell}\in\mathbb{R}^{m_{\ell}\times m_{\ell}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\delta,\ell}\in\mathbb{R}^{m_{\ell}\times m_{\ell}}</annotation></semantics></math>. For modern neural networks, the dimensions <math id="A6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> can be in the thousands for typical transformer layers, and can even reach the millions in domains like high-resolution computer vision or for layers tied to large vocabularies. This makes the direct formation and manipulation of these matrices computationally infeasible due to both memory and time constraints. To overcome this, we employ a memory-efficient approximation scheme that avoids forming these large matrices entirely.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The core strategy is to approximate the true second moment matrices using statistics gathered from a small, representative batch of <math id="A6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> data samples, which we refer to as a probe dataset. We perform a single forward and backward pass through the model for these <math id="A6.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> samples to collect the corresponding inputs and upstream gradients for each layer <math id="A6.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>. These are stacked column-wise to form two tall-and-thin probe matrices:</p>
<table id="A6.Ex47" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex47.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\ell}=[h_{\ell-1}(z_{1}),\dots,h_{\ell-1}(z_{N})]\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{\ell}\times N}\quad\text{and}\quad\Delta_{\ell}=[\delta_{\ell}(z_{1}),\dots,\delta_{\ell}(z_{N})]\in\mathbb{R}^{m_{\ell}\times N}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mtext>and</mtext><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\ell}=[h_{\ell-1}(z_{1}),\dots,h_{\ell-1}(z_{N})]\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{\ell}\times N}\quad\text{and}\quad\Delta_{\ell}=[\delta_{\ell}(z_{1}),\dots,\delta_{\ell}(z_{N})]\in\mathbb{R}^{m_{\ell}\times N}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.p2.2" class="ltx_p">With these probe matrices, we can approximate the full second moment matrices as <math id="A6.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{h,\ell}\approx\frac{1}{N}H_{\ell}H_{\ell}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{h,\ell}\approx\frac{1}{N}H_{\ell}H_{\ell}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\delta,\ell}\approx\frac{1}{N}\Delta_{\ell}\Delta_{\ell}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\delta,\ell}\approx\frac{1}{N}\Delta_{\ell}\Delta_{\ell}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>. Instead of computing these prohibitively large second moment matrices, the key insight is to directly compute the "skinny" Singular Value Decompositions of the much smaller probe matrices:</p>
<table id="A6.Ex48" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex48.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\ell}=U_{H,\ell}\Sigma_{H,\ell}V_{H,\ell}^{\top}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\Delta_{\ell}=U_{\Delta,\ell}\Sigma_{\Delta,\ell}V_{\Delta,\ell}^{\top}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mspace style="width:2em;" width="2em"></mspace><mtext>and</mtext><mspace style="width:2em;" width="2em"></mspace><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\ell}=U_{H,\ell}\Sigma_{H,\ell}V_{H,\ell}^{\top}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\Delta_{\ell}=U_{\Delta,\ell}\Sigma_{\Delta,\ell}V_{\Delta,\ell}^{\top},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.p2.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A6.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{H,\ell}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{\ell}\times N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{H,\ell}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{\ell}\times N}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma_{H,\ell}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma_{H,\ell}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{H,\ell}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{H,\ell}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}</annotation></semantics></math>, and similarly for the decomposition of <math id="A6.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>. This decomposition is the key to bypassing the expensive computations, as we can express the regularized square roots of the approximate second moment matrices without ever forming the full matrices. For example, for <math id="A6.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{h,\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{h,\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="A6.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(C_{h,\ell}+\lambda I)^{1/2}\approx(\frac{1}{N}H_{\ell}H_{\ell}^{\top}+\lambda I)^{1/2}=(\frac{1}{N}U_{H,\ell}\Sigma_{H,\ell}^{2}U_{H,\ell}^{\top}+\lambda I)^{1/2}=U_{H,\ell}(\frac{1}{N}\Sigma_{H,\ell}^{2}+\lambda I)^{1/2}U_{H,\ell}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>≈</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(C_{h,\ell}+\lambda I)^{1/2}\approx(\frac{1}{N}H_{\ell}H_{\ell}^{\top}+\lambda I)^{1/2}=(\frac{1}{N}U_{H,\ell}\Sigma_{H,\ell}^{2}U_{H,\ell}^{\top}+\lambda I)^{1/2}=U_{H,\ell}(\frac{1}{N}\Sigma_{H,\ell}^{2}+\lambda I)^{1/2}U_{H,\ell}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>. We then define the small, diagonal matrices that hold the regularized singular values:</p>
<table id="A6.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{H,\ell}\triangleq\left(\frac{1}{N}\Sigma_{H,\ell}^{2}+\lambda I\right)^{1/2}\qquad\text{and}\qquad D_{\Delta,\ell}\triangleq\left(\frac{1}{N}\Sigma_{\Delta,\ell}^{2}+\lambda I\right)^{1/2}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>≜</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mspace style="width:2em;" width="2em"></mspace><mtext>and</mtext><mspace style="width:2em;" width="2em"></mspace><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>≜</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{H,\ell}\triangleq\left(\frac{1}{N}\Sigma_{H,\ell}^{2}+\lambda I\right)^{1/2}\qquad\text{and}\qquad D_{\Delta,\ell}\triangleq\left(\frac{1}{N}\Sigma_{\Delta,\ell}^{2}+\lambda I\right)^{1/2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="A6.p2.4" class="ltx_p">The required reweighting transformations are thus efficiently represented as <math id="A6.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{h,\ell,\lambda}^{1/2}\approx U_{H,\ell}D_{H,\ell}U_{H,\ell}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>≈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{h,\ell,\lambda}^{1/2}\approx U_{H,\ell}D_{H,\ell}U_{H,\ell}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\delta,\ell,\lambda}^{1/2}\approx U_{\Delta,\ell}D_{\Delta,\ell}U_{\Delta,\ell}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>≈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\delta,\ell,\lambda}^{1/2}\approx U_{\Delta,\ell}D_{\Delta,\ell}U_{\Delta,\ell}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>. Substituting these efficient representations into the definition of the data-aware matrix <math id="A6.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{\ell}=C_{\delta,\ell}^{1/2}W_{\ell}C_{h,\ell}^{1/2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{\ell}=C_{\delta,\ell}^{1/2}W_{\ell}C_{h,\ell}^{1/2}</annotation></semantics></math> reveals the final computational trick:</p>
