<p id="A6.p2.5" class="ltx_p">This shows that the SVD of the very large matrix <math id="A6.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> is directly related to the SVD of the small core matrix <math id="A6.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{\text{core},\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mtext>core</mtext><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{\text{core},\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>, which has dimensions at most <math id="A6.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\times N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\times N</annotation></semantics></math>. We compute the SVD of this core matrix, <math id="A6.p2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{\text{core},\ell}=P_{\ell}\Sigma_{\ell}Q_{\ell}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mtext>core</mtext><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{\text{core},\ell}=P_{\ell}\Sigma_{\ell}Q_{\ell}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>, and truncate it to the desired rank <math id="A6.p2.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> by selecting the top <math id="A6.p2.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> columns of <math id="A6.p2.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.p2.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> (denoted <math id="A6.p2.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\ell,r},Q_{\ell,r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\ell,r},Q_{\ell,r}</annotation></semantics></math>) and the top-left <math id="A6.p2.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\ell}\times r_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\ell}\times r_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> block of <math id="A6.p2.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> (denoted <math id="A6.p2.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma_{\ell,r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma_{\ell,r}</annotation></semantics></math>). The optimal low-rank approximation <math id="A6.p2.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{W}_{\ell}^{\star}=A_{\ell}^{\star}B_{\ell}^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>W</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{W}_{\ell}^{\star}=A_{\ell}^{\star}B_{\ell}^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> is constructed by transforming the truncated SVD of the core matrix back into the original weight space. This yields numerically stable, closed-form expressions for the low-rank matrices <math id="A6.p2.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{\ell}^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{\ell}^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.p2.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{\ell}^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{\ell}^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> without ever forming the full <math id="A6.p2.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{W}_{\ell}^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>W</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{W}_{\ell}^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> matrix:</p>
<table id="A6.E14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{\ell}^{\star}=U_{\Delta,\ell}D_{\Delta,\ell}^{-1}P_{\ell,r}\Sigma_{\ell,r}^{1/2}\qquad\text{and}\qquad B_{\ell}^{\star}=\Sigma_{\ell,r}^{1/2}Q_{\ell,r}^{\top}D_{H,\ell}^{-1}U_{H,\ell}^{\top}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mspace style="width:2em;" width="2em"></mspace><mtext>and</mtext><mspace style="width:2em;" width="2em"></mspace><mrow><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>,</mo><mi encoding="application/x-tex">A_{\ell}^{\star}=U_{\Delta,\ell}D_{\Delta,\ell}^{-1}P_{\ell,r}\Sigma_{\ell,r}^{1/2}\qquad\text{and}\qquad B_{\ell}^{\star}=\Sigma_{\ell,r}^{1/2}Q_{\ell,r}^{\top}D_{H,\ell}^{-1}U_{H,\ell}^{\top}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(14)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.p2.6" class="ltx_p">All computationally intensive steps are now performed on matrices whose dimensions are related to the small probe set size <math id="A6.p2.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>, not the target model dimensions <math id="A6.p2.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.p2.m33" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>. This entire procedure is highly efficient, assuming <math id="A6.p2.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\ll\min(n_{\ell},m_{\ell})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≪</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\ll\min(n_{\ell},m_{\ell})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.p2.m35" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\ell}\leq N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\ell}\leq N</annotation></semantics></math>. For each layer, the complexity is composed of a single forward and backward pass for <math id="A6.p2.m36" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> samples, two skinny SVDs of the probe matrices with complexity <math id="A6.p2.m37" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(n_{\ell}N^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(n_{\ell}N^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.p2.m38" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(m_{\ell}N^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(m_{\ell}N^{2})</annotation></semantics></math>, the formation of the core matrix which costs <math id="A6.p2.m39" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(m_{\ell}n_{\ell}N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(m_{\ell}n_{\ell}N)</annotation></semantics></math>, an SVD of the small core matrix with complexity <math id="A6.p2.m40" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(N^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>N</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(N^{3})</annotation></semantics></math>, and the final factor construction which costs <math id="A6.p2.m41" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(m_{\ell}Nr_{\ell})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(m_{\ell}Nr_{\ell})</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A6.p2.m42" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{\ell}^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{\ell}^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.p2.m43" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(n_{\ell}Nr_{\ell})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(n_{\ell}Nr_{\ell})</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A6.p2.m44" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{\ell}^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{\ell}^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math>. The dominant costs are the core matrix formation and the skinny SVDs, which is a dramatic reduction from the <math id="A6.p2.m45" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\min(m_{\ell},n_{\ell})^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\min(m_{\ell},n_{\ell})^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> complexity required for the SVD of the full second moment matrices.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
